memory_update.text: POWL should be promoted to the primary underfollowed lane for the transformers/switchgear/power-quality node because its medium-voltage switchgear, electrical houses, utility orders, data-center orders, and backlog directly match the bottleneck hypothesis.
BELFB is a component-level hypothesis for custom magnetics, power conversion, and data-center/networking power products; exposure needs revenue materiality verification before surviving later layers.
PLPC is a speculative shadow candidate adjacent to the node, best treated as transmission/distribution hardware exposure rather than transformer or switchgear exposure.

The investable US-listed universe for direct transformer pure plays appears thin; the better Layer 1B path is switchgear/electrical distribution systems, custom magnetics, power components, transmission hardware, and diversified utility-equipment references.

Need a follow-up pass on transformer-specific US-listed exposure, including whether any OTC foreign listings, private suppliers, or transformer-heavy divisions inside diversified companies create measurable public-market exposure.

node: Transformers, switchgear, power quality products, and electrical distribution magnetics
summary: Layer 1B expansion for the transformer/switchgear/power-quality node finds one obvious reference name and three underfollowed or shadow candidates. The clearest US-listed underfollowed exposure is Powell Industries, where medium-voltage switchgear, electrical houses, utility/data-center orders, and backlog directly map to the node. Bel Fuse is a smaller custom magnetics/power-conversion hypothesis tied to data-center/networking power and magnetic components rather than utility-scale transformers. Preformed Line Products is a second-order transmission/distribution hardware shadow candidate: not a transformer or switchgear company, but potentially levered to the same grid buildout and line-equipment procurement bottleneck. Hubbell is included as a larger reference comp because its Utility Solutions and Power Systems offerings overlap transmission, distribution, and medium-voltage switchgear, but its size and diversification make it less suitable for the underfollowed lane.
